1. `lem-derivative-of-det-i-minus-xa` — [Statement and proof step 1.2](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/lem-derivative-of-det-i-minus-xa.md:27)

   The expression
   \[
   \operatorname{tr}_R(\operatorname{adj}(M(x))A)
   \]
   applies \(\operatorname{tr}_R\) outside its declared domain: \(M(x)\), its adjugate, and their product with \(A\) have entries in \(R[x]\subseteq R\llbracket x\rrbracket\), not \(R\).

   Evidence: `def-trace-of-a-square-matrix-over-a-commutative-ring` defines
   > “Let \(R\) be a commutative ring … and \(A\in M_p(R)\). The trace of \(A\) over \(R\) is \(\operatorname{tr}_R(A):=\sum_{i<p}a_{ii}\).”

   The intended identity is valid after using the trace over \(R[x]\) or \(R\llbracket x\rrbracket\), or after explicitly defining coefficientwise extension. This is a sub-30-second type/notation repair, so **nonfatal**.

2. `cor-closed-walk-trace-generating-functions` — [first displayed identity and proof steps 1.1–2.1](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/cor-closed-walk-trace-generating-functions.md:27)

   The same domain mismatch propagates to
   \[
   \operatorname{tr}_R(\operatorname{adj}(I_p-xA))
   \quad\text{and}\quad
   \operatorname{tr}_R(M^{-1}A),
   \]
   whose arguments lie respectively in \(M_p(R[x])\) and \(M_p(R\llbracket x\rrbracket)\). The occurrences \(\operatorname{tr}_R(A^n)\) are correctly typed.

   The cited trace definition has only the \(M_p(R)\to R\) domain quoted above. Relabeling the series-valued traces by their actual coefficient rings makes the proof correct. **Nonfatal**.
